claims.quote: achieving up to 4x better end-to-end performance than the RocksDB system under various settings
in the read-heavy workload (Figure 6 (a)), Aggressive is the most effective

claims.metric: RusKey converged policy, read-heavy and write-heavy
claims.quote: Lerp selects an aggressive compaction policy with a read-heavy workload and a lazy compaction policy with a write-heavy workload
Lerp selects an intermediate policy K = 4 on the balanced workload, which dominates all baselines after around 600 missions
its performance is relatively better than the other two baselines on the balanced workload

claims.metric: missions to converge, read-heavy and write-heavy
claims.quote: it takes Lerp around 300 missions to explore and navigate to the optimal setting with the read-heavy and write-heavy workloads

claims.metric: no single fixed policy is best on every workload
claims.quote: the baselines perform sub-optimally on at least one workload

claims.metric: RusKey average performance ranking, dynamic workload
claims.quote: it achieves a high average ranking of 1.2
RusKey achieves up to 4 times better performance than Aggressive (on the write-heavy session)
up to 2.4 times better performance than Moderate (on the read-heavy session)
RusKey adopts compaction policy settings of K = 1, K = 5, K = 10, K = 6, K = 2 on the read-heavy, balanced, write-heavy, write-incline and read-inclined sessions, respectively

claims.metric: end-to-end time, greedy / lazy / flexible transition
claims.quote: the greedy transition, lazy transition and flexible transition use 51s, 44s, and 40s, respectively
